layers.note: Loose mats in rock crevices and on gravel among the boulders.

moisture.note: Dry rock; it dries and curls, and greens after rain.

heat_load.note: Rock crevices, often on cooler, shaded faces.

elevation_m.note: 600 to 2,000 m (Flora of North America); 2,000 to 4,500 feet in Arizona (Kearney and Peebles).

shade_tolerance.note: Sun to the shade of boulders and ledges.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 3 to 14 °C; gone below 0 °C and above 17 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −12 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −17 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 24 to 33 °C; gone below 21 °C, where summers are too short, and above 35 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 4,500 to 9,500 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 3,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 2,800 to 7,600 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 2,000.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.08 to 0.45, gone by 0.04 and above 0.6.

summer_rain.note: Needs the monsoon's summer rain: from about 0.3 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone below 0.2; up to about 0.75, gone by 0.85.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m, 32.25 N 111.17 W) from general knowledge of the species and the ranges, habitats and elevations in the sources read for its spec (2026-10-19). Arizona spikemoss grows in Arizona, western Texas, Baja California and Sonora, on sandstone, igneous or rarely limestone rock (Flora of North America; Kearney and Peebles). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records; every full range holds the bajada's climate (coldest month about 11 °C, warmest about 31 °C, about 7,600 degree-days above 0 °C, coldest night about −4 °C, moisture index about 0.15, about half the year's rain in summer).
